# Give the model (fallback chain) config control over the free-tier request budget

discovered-from:LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20

## Goal (user story)

As the proxy operator, I want to set the free-tier request-budget behaviour
**per model / fallback chain** (with sensible global defaults), so I can tune
`plan`, `author`, `code` and `compact` independently — instead of every model
inheriting one global setting — while any single provider entry can still
override its own behaviour.

## Current state

- `rate_limit_rpm` is a **provider-entry** field (`provider_cfg`), so it is
  already configurable per entry — today only `munitoai-free` sets it (10).
- The four *behaviour* knobs are read **server-wide only**:
  `server.provider_rate_limit_reserve_ratio`,
  `server.provider_rate_limit_wait_max_seconds`,
  `server.provider_rate_limit_wait_max_waiters`,
  `server.provider_affinity_ttl_seconds`
  (`proxy/proxy/provider_budget.py::_config_value`, called with the server
  config).
- `acquire_provider_budget(provider_cfg, config, session_id, request)` is **not**
  given `model_config`/the model name, so a model-scoped setting cannot be
  expressed today — a single reserve ratio / wait cap applies to all chains.
- `affinity_ttl_seconds` is applied in three places, all of which read the same
  server config today: `acquire_provider_budget()`,
  `record_provider_affinity()` (via `provider.py::_maybe_record_provider_affinity`)
  and `provider_affinity_active()`. Honouring a model-scoped TTL (AC1) therefore
  requires threading the model config into the affinity record/lookup path too,
  not only into the acquire call.
- Both budget call sites in `proxy/proxy/provider.py` are
  `_proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle` (~line 7128) and
  `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle` (~line 8141); each already holds the request's
  `model_config`.
- Consequence: an interactive chain (e.g. `plan`) and a background chain (e.g.
  `compact`) cannot trade latency against free-tier utilisation differently, and
  a future gated entry cannot be tuned without changing global behaviour.
- Caveat on `compact`: `models.compact` is consumed only by
  `proxy/proxy/compaction_summarizer.py`, which dispatches to its providers
  directly over httpx and never calls the gate. A `models.compact.budget` block
  is therefore accepted and resolvable but has **no runtime effect** until that
  dispatch is gated (tracked separately — see OPEN QUESTION 1).

## Desired change

Add a **model-level `budget` block** with precedence
**provider entry > model block > server default > built-in default**:

```yaml
models:
  plan:
    budget:
      reserve_ratio: 0.4        # share of rate_limit_rpm reserved for in-progress
      wait_max_seconds: 10      # per-request wait cap for in-progress sessions
      max_waiters: 4            # concurrent waiter cap
      affinity_ttl_seconds: 600 # how long a session counts as in-progress
    providers:
      - name: munitoai-free
        rate_limit_rpm: 15      # entry-level override of the budget size
        budget:                 # optional per-entry behaviour override
          reserve_ratio: 0.2
```

- All five keys are optional at every layer; absent keys fall through to the next
  layer, so **existing configs behave exactly as today**.
- Values are clamped/validated exactly as the server-level knobs are today
  (ratio to `[0,1]`, wait/TTL to `>= 0`, malformed values fall back to the
  default with a warning — fail open, never fail closed).
- The effective values are visible per request in the budget logs/attempt
  diagnostics (which layer supplied `reserve_slots`/`effective_limit`), and the
  provider diagnostics table keeps showing remaining/limit per entry.
- The budget **bucket** remains keyed by provider entry (one account quota shared
  by `plan`/`author`/`code` even when their model blocks differ) — document this
  explicitly so per-model tuning is not mistaken for per-model quota.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A `models.<name>.budget` block is honoured for `reserve_ratio`,
   `wait_max_seconds`, `max_waiters` and `affinity_ttl_seconds`, and a provider
   entry may override any of them with its own `budget` block.
2. Precedence is exactly entry > model > server > built-in default, proven by
   tests for every key (single-layer and multi-layer combinations).
3. Omitting all blocks reproduces today's behaviour byte-for-byte — identical
   `BudgetDecision` values (`reserve_slots`, `effective_limit`, `reason`) and
   identical log lines for the shipped `config.yaml` (no behavioural change;
   tested).
4. Malformed/out-of-range values fall back to the next layer with a logged
   warning and never raise or block a request (tests for each key).
5. The budget bucket stays shared per provider entry across models; a test proves
   two models with different `budget` blocks still consume one `rate_limit_rpm`
   window.
6. The effective configuration is visible in the budget skip/wait log lines and
   the attempt diagnostics (source layer included), and the provider diagnostics
   table keeps showing remaining/limit.
7. Tests cover both real fallback entry points —
   `_proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle` and `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle` —
   proving each passes the request's model config into the gate. (The intake's
   third clause, "the compaction/summarizer path where it reaches the same
   gate", is **not implementable as written**: `models.compact` is consumed only
   by `build_compact_summarizer()`, which calls providers directly over httpx
   and never reaches the gate. See OPEN QUESTION 1 and the follow-up item.)
8. Documentation updated: `proxy/config.yaml` header comments + a commented
   example, `proxy/README.md`, `proxy/docs/routing.md`, `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md`
   (model-level `budget` block alongside the `providers` list).
9. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Config-shape only: no change to gate semantics, reserve maths, or the
  affinity/wait design.
- Keep every layer optional; no migration of existing configs required.
- Do not introduce per-model *quota* (a separate budget per model) — that would
  break the one-account-per-entry model; if it is ever wanted, it must be a
  separate decision.
- The gate must remain fail-open when the new blocks are absent or malformed.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/provider_budget.py` — resolve each knob through the new
  entry > model > server precedence; extend `BudgetDecision`/logs with the source
  layer.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — pass `model_config` (and the model key) into
  `acquire_provider_budget()` from both fallback entry points
  (`_proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle`, `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle`) and into
  `_maybe_record_provider_affinity()` so the recorded TTL matches the model.
- `proxy/tests/test_provider_budget.py` — precedence/validation/shared-bucket
  tests, plus the call-site wiring test (the module already imports
  `proxy.provider as provider`, so no new test module is needed).
- `proxy/config.yaml` — document the `models.<name>.budget` block; commented
  example.
- `proxy/tests/test_config_merge.py` + fixtures — only if the new keys are
  introduced as shipped values (they are optional; likely no fixture change).
- `proxy/README.md`, `proxy/docs/routing.md`, `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md` — docs.

## Implementation order (test-first)

1. Add failing tests in `proxy/tests/test_provider_budget.py` for precedence,
   validation/fallback and the shared-bucket guarantee (AC1–AC5).
2. Implement the layered resolver in `proxy/proxy/provider_budget.py`
   (entry > model > server > built-in) and extend `BudgetDecision`/log lines
   with the source layer (AC6).
3. Thread `model_config` through both `provider.py` call sites and the affinity
   record/lookup path (AC1 `affinity_ttl_seconds`, AC7).
4. Update docs: `proxy/config.yaml`, `proxy/README.md`,
   `proxy/docs/routing.md`, `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md` (AC8).
5. Run the suite via the test skill (AC9).

## OPEN QUESTIONS

1. **Compaction/summarizer path and the budget gate.** AC7 originally asked for
   coverage of "the compaction/summarizer path where it reaches the same gate".
   Fact check (this session): `proxy/proxy/compaction_summarizer.py`
   (`build_compact_summarizer` / `_remote_chat_url`) resolves
   `models.compact.providers` itself and calls each provider **directly over
   httpx**, bypassing `localhost:8080` — so it never reaches
   `acquire_provider_budget()` and no `budget` block applies to it.
   AC7 was therefore narrowed to the two real fallback entry points and the gap
   was filed as `LP-0MVFYYYXS0011T58` (Gate the models.compact summarizer
   dispatch through the provider budget).
   **Preferred option (a): accept the split** — it preserves the "config-shape
   only" constraint and leaves eight of nine ACs unblocked; the summarizer gate
   is tracked separately. Alternative (b): widen this item to gate the
   summarizer dispatch as well (larger effort, and the `compact` half of the
   user story only becomes real then). Producer decision requested — see the
   comment on this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Is `rate_limit_rpm` used for any other provider (would per-model tuning
  matter beyond the free tier)?" Answer (Map, 2026-10-18, comment
  `LP-C0MVDVL1IR002EH5X`): no — `munitoai-free` is the only entry declaring it;
  the capability is dormant for every other provider, and the bucket is keyed by
  provider entry so `plan`/`author`/`code` share one 10/min window.
- Q: "Do both `provider.py` budget call sites have `model_config` available, and
  what are the functions called?" Answer (this session, code inspection): yes —
  `_proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle` (~line 7128) and
  `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle` (~line 8145); the AC7 name `_proxy_with_fallback`
  was corrected accordingly.
- OPEN QUESTION 1 (compaction/summarizer gate) — see above; needs a producer
  decision before the item is implemented. It does not block the other eight
  ACs.

## Related work

- `LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20` — reserve + 15 s wait cap (introduced the knobs this item
  makes per-model).
- `LP-0MVDQ1GMO00801PL` — the original budget gate.
- `LP-0MVDVJYN5001BMG4` — evaluating whether the `munitoai-free` budget itself
  should be raised (the first consumer of per-model tuning).
- `LP-0MVDQKF4F008LGS6` — restricting the free tier to cheap mode (another
  model-scoped policy that could share this configuration shape).
- `LP-0MVDUZ0E10011W3C` (in progress) — rewrites the limiter/budget skip log
  lines that AC6 extends; sequence with it so the two log changes do not
  conflict.
- `LP-0MVDW6Z870066DEY` (open) — consolidating the fallback-chain configuration
  docs, of which the `budget` block docs (AC8) are one part.
- `LP-0MVF2DNCX003Z5CO` (in progress) — per-model context size, an existing
  example of a model-level knob read per request.
- Follow-up (filed this session) — `LP-0MVFYYYXS0011T58` — gate the
  `models.compact` summarizer dispatch so a `budget` block has runtime effect
  there.

# Intake Brief: Web UI to log input and output tokens (LP-0MVE592AU008VAP4)

## Headline

Display a cumulative, cross-request per-model token summary (input + output, broken down by category) in the existing `/logs` page summary header, using the current SSE token-snapshot and JSON-persistence plumbing.

---

## Problem Statement

The proxy's `/logs` page displays per-endpoint token totals and per-category breakdowns, but there is no view that aggregates token usage across all endpoints by LLM model. Operators cannot see how much each model is consuming overall — a key cost and capacity signal.

---

## Users

**Primary:** Proxy operators monitoring LLM proxy activity via the web log UI, diagnosing cost drivers and capacity allocation across models.

**User Stories:**
- As a proxy operator, I want a per-model running total of input (sent) and output (recv) tokens in the `/logs` summary header, so I can quickly see which models are consuming the most.
- As a proxy operator, I want each model's total broken down by category (User messages, Assistant, Tool Calls, System Prompt + Response), so I can attribute costs more precisely than a single aggregate number.
- As a proxy operator, I want the running totals to persist across proxy restarts, so I get a true long-term view rather than a reset-per-restart snapshot.

---

## Acceptance Criteria

- The `/logs` page summary header displays a **per-model token section** (in addition to the existing per-endpoint section) showing:
  - One row per distinct model, with a total sent (input) and total recv (output) for that model.
  - Per-model category breakdown: User messages, Assistant (sent), Tool Calls (sent), System Prompt (sent), Response (recv).
  - Model names extracted from existing token-count keys (the `-> model:<name>` suffix already present in token-count keys such as `sent:user:POST /v1/chat/completions -> model:qwen3.6`).
- Running totals accumulate across requests and **persist across proxy restarts** via the existing `token_counts` JSON file (`proxy/logs/token_counts.json`).
- Category counts are consistent with the existing per-category breakdown keys (`sent:user:*`, `sent:assistant:*`, `sent:tool:*`, `sent:system:*`, `recv:response:*`) — no new token-counting logic is introduced.
- The per-model summary renders within the existing `renderSummary()` JavaScript function in `view_logs.html`, using the same SSE snapshot format (`{"tokens": {...}}`).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

---

## Constraints

- Must **reuse** the existing token-count key structure and SSE broadcast path — no new server-side token-counting logic.
- Must not break or double-count the existing per-endpoint display.
- Must handle the case where multiple endpoint paths share the same model name (aggregate correctly).
- Must be backward-compatible — no changes to the `token_counts` JSON schema; model grouping is a **UI-side** concern.

---

## Existing State

- `proxy/proxy/observability.py` — `srv.token_counts` dict holds keys like `sent:user:POST /v1/chat/completions -> model:qwen3.6`; `_increment_tokens()` updates these; `broadcast_status()` pushes snapshots via SSE.
- `proxy/templates/view_logs.html` — `renderSummary()` iterates endpoint defs and matches keys against endpoint paths; per-category breakdown already displayed per endpoint.
- Token counts are persisted to `proxy/logs/token_counts.json` (or `token_counts_filename`), loaded at startup via `load_token_counts()`.
- The model name is already encoded in token-count keys as the `-> model:<name>` suffix (visible in log output and keys).

---

## Desired Change

1. **Update `renderSummary()` in `view_logs.html`** to group token-count keys by model name (extract `-> model:<name>` from each key) and render a per-model table with sent/recv totals and category breakdowns.
2. **No server-side changes** — model grouping is a pure client-side aggregation over the existing token-snapshot data.

**Key Files:**
- `proxy/templates/view_logs.html` — `renderSummary()` to add per-model section to summary header
- `proxy/proxy/observability.py` — No changes expected (existing SSE broadcast already carries per-key data)

---

## Related Work

| Item | Title | Relationship |
|------|-------|--------------|
| LP-0MRAW8XUF005IB4K | Token breakdown by category in session log display | Completed — established the per-category token-count keys and per-endpoint display this feature builds on |
| LP-0MQ0PYH8P008DLPJ | Web based logging per provider/model/session | Completed — parent of the log viewer feature set |
| LP-0MRAG775K008CKDG | Rethink logs display: remove model tabs, flat session list | Completed — current log viewer layout |

---

## Risks & Assumptions

| Risk | Mitigation |
|------|-----------|
| Some token-count keys may lack the `-> model:` suffix (e.g. from legacy data or non-chat endpoints) | Keys without a model name are grouped under "unknown" with a debug log entry |
| Scope creep (adding per-model charts, export, or filters) | Record additional feature ideas as separate work items linked to this item |
| UI becomes crowded with many models | Use a scrollable card/container; add a "show fewer models" toggle if needed |

---

## Assumptions

- The model name in the key suffix is stable and sufficient for grouping (no need to fetch from a separate model-registry).
- The existing `token_counts` file is loaded at startup and retained across restarts — no migration needed.
- The proxy's `/logs` page is the sole UI target; no changes to the TUI footer or other dashboards.

---

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q1: "Where should the per-model running total appear?" — Answer (operator): **A — In the existing `/logs` page summary header, alongside the current per-endpoint display**. Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q2: "What does 'running total' mean for persistence/scope?" — Answer (operator): **A — Cumulative since recording began, persisted across proxy restarts**. Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q3: "What granularity per model?" — Answer (operator): **B — Per-model totals broken down by category (user/assistant/tool/system) as well**. Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.

## Problem statement

The proxy's `low` priority route (used by the priority-window cheap slot, 01:00–10:00 local, plus any explicit `X-Priority: low`) currently chains as `[local-qwen3, munitoai-free]` for the plan/author/code models. When the 2 local slots are saturated (a common overnight condition — see the 2026-10-19 proxy-usage-analysis report: `fallback_after_queue` 1657, `large_context_bypass` 1530, `context_too_large` 3393), low-priority traffic falls straight through to `munitoai-free`, which is capped at **`rate_limit_rpm: 2`** and is the last entry in the chain — so once its tiny budget is spent the request has nowhere else to go but an upstream 429 (16 upstream 429 events in the last window, all from `api.munito.ai`).

Meanwhile the three `opencode-go` entries (`opencode-go-3`, `opencode-go-2`, `opencode-go`) sit idle despite being available during their off-peak UTC windows (`["00:00-01:00", "04:00-06:00", "10:00-00:00"]`, added by LP-0MSXPHTD9004DZ4P) — which are precisely the hours when the cheap priority window is active and local is most contended.

Goal: allow low-priority work to fall back to **all** opencode models while they are inside their permissible (`available_times`) windows, so local-slot overflow during cheap hours is absorbed by idle paid capacity instead of being rate-limited on the free tier.

## Operator decisions (recorded)

- **Do NOT widen `available_times`.** The existing off-peak windows stay exactly as they are; paid spend remains confined to them.
- **Allow all opencode models on the low chain**, gated by those windows — not just one entry.

## Context / constraints

- `priority_routes.low` for plan/author/code is `[local-qwen3, munitoai-free]` (`proxy/config.yaml`); `munitoai-free` carries `rate_limit_rpm: 2`.
- Each of plan/author/code defines three equivalent opencode entries: `opencode-go-3` (OPENCODE_3_API_KEY), `opencode-go-2` (OPENCODE_2_API_KEY), `opencode-go` (OPENCODE_API_KEY) — same gateway, same model `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, same windows.
- **Why all three is meaningful (not cosmetic):** per LP-0MSMBWB23009XYPW / LP-0MVCX0E2V001VB5N, rate-limit quarantine is keyed on the **API-key account** (`_usage_limit_account_key` = `api_key_env@endpoint`), *not* the shared gateway domain. A 429 on one entry therefore poisons only that account, so its sibling keys are still tried with their own independent quota — i.e. 3× rate-limit capacity.
- **Counter-caveat to document:** for *non-rate-limit* failures (5xx, stalls) same-gateway siblings ARE skipped as one failure domain (`_failure_domain_key` / `attempted_domains`), so the three entries do **not** multiply capacity during an opencode outage. That is correct behaviour and must be stated in the config comments so nobody expects 3× resilience.
- **UTC-vs-local alignment (measured):** `available_times` are **UTC**; the cheap window (01:00–10:00) is **local `Europe/Dublin` = UTC 00:00–09:00**. opencode-go is unavailable UTC 01:00–04:00 and 06:00–10:00, so the new tiers add capacity in **~3 of the 9 cheap hours** (UTC 00:00–01:00 and 04:00–06:00). Accepted — the gaps are deliberate paid-spend avoidance, and the operator chose not to widen them.
- The `compact` model's low chain (`opencode-go-compact → deepseek-flash-compact`) is out of scope.
- The fully-paid `munitoai` and `deepseek-flash` entries must NOT join the low chain — they have no window discipline enforcing off-peak-only spend (`munitoai` has no `available_times` at all).

## Scope

Config + routing documentation + tests only. No llama-server changes, no `available_times` changes. Evidence via the proxy-usage-analysis skill (`python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py --hours 24`).

## Acceptance criteria

# Retire guessed usage-limit reset for opencode accounts using /v1/usage seconds_to_reset

## Goal

Replace the *guessed* reset time used for `GoUsageLimitError` quarantine
(`provider._usage_limit_reset_info`, LP-0MUQTCMW2001VXH8) with the
authoritative `monthly.resetsAt` seconds available from the `/v1/usage` poll
introduced by LP-0MVF4FIP1001RD8P, for `opencode-*` accounts.

## Scope

- For `opencode-*` accounts with a fresh quota snapshot, use the derived
  `seconds_to_reset` from the poller instead of the rolled-dice
  `_usage_limit_guess_cap_seconds` / `_parse_resets_in` path when a
  `GoUsageLimitError` is observed.
- Keep the guessing path for non-`opencode-*` accounts (no quota source).
- Guard: if the snapshot is stale or absent, fall back to the existing guess so
  behaviour never blocks on missing quota state.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — A `GoUsageLimitError` on an `opencode-*` account with a fresh snapshot quarantines for exactly the snapshot's `seconds_to_reset` (+ configured margin), asserted in a test that fakes the error and a known snapshot.
- AC2 — With a stale or absent snapshot the existing guessing path is used unchanged (regression: current `test_usage_limit_reset.py` cases still pass).
- AC3 — The obsolete guessed-reset code paths for these accounts are removed or clearly marked dead, and the change is documented here. Clarification: because AC2 keeps the guess as the stale/absent fallback, "removed or marked dead" means the guessed branch is unreachable for an `opencode-*` account with a fresh snapshot; it is retained — and documented as fallback-only — for every other case. No other reset behaviour is retired.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_usage_limit_reset_info`,
  `_usage_limit_reset_seconds`, `_usage_limit_guess_cap_seconds`,
  `_parse_resets_in`, `_set_usage_limit_quarantine`, and the two 429 call sites
  (≈ lines 7277 and 8606).
- `proxy/proxy/quota_state.py` — `get_quota_snapshot`, `quota_behaviour`,
  `quota_state_max_age_seconds`, `QuotaSnapshot.seconds_to_reset`.
- `proxy/tests/test_usage_limit_reset.py` — unit + end-to-end regression tests.
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — usage-limit quarantine contract (guessed-vs-explicit
  reset, margins, account key).
- `docs/dev/quota-surge.md` — quota-surge design doc reference section.

## Dependencies

- Depends on `Quota poller and derived state (tracer bullet)`
  (LP-0MVF7KEG7007C8MF) — dependency edge recorded in Worklog.
- The poller is already on `dev` (commits f7015f35, 41ef041e, 05d37fe7), so the
  previously stated "blocked on the parent epic shipping to `dev`" condition is
  satisfied on `dev`; the `dev`→`main` release is a ship-skill concern and does
  not block implementation.

## Minimal Implementation

1. **Tests first** (`proxy/tests/test_usage_limit_reset.py`), injecting a known
   snapshot via `quota_state.snapshot_from_usage` + `quota_state.set_clock` and
   resetting state in fixtures:
   - a `GoUsageLimitError` 429 on an `opencode-*` entry with a fresh snapshot →
     quarantine equals `snapshot.seconds_to_reset + 120 s`;
   - the same with a stale snapshot (older than
     `server.quota_state_max_age_seconds`) → existing guessed/explicit path;
   - the same with no snapshot at all → existing path (AC2 regression);
   - a non-`opencode-*` entry with a snapshot present → unaffected (guess or
     explicit message path).
2. Add a resolver in `proxy/provider.py` (e.g.
   `_quota_snapshot_reset_seconds(provider_cfg, config)`) that returns the
   authoritative reset or `None`, gated by `quota_state.quota_behaviour(...)`
   (kill switch / staleness) so a disabled or stale quota source never changes
   reset behaviour.
3. Thread `provider_cfg` + `config` into `_usage_limit_reset_info` (both 429
   call sites already hold both) and prefer the snapshot-derived value for
   `opencode-*` entries when it is fresh and positive; otherwise keep the
   current `_parse_resets_in` → `metadata.limitName` guess → `None` cascade
   unchanged.
4. Mark the guessed branch fallback-only in the `_usage_limit_reset_info` /
   `_usage_limit_guess_cap_seconds` docstrings and update the `Resets`/guess
   paragraphs in `proxy/docs/routing.md` (retirement note in
   `docs/dev/quota-surge.md` §References/§interaction text).
5. Keep the existing 2-minute `_USAGE_LIMIT_RESET_MARGIN_SECONDS` margin, the
   `_usage_limit_account_key` quarantine key and `explicit=True` semantics
   untouched; log the source used (snapshot vs. message vs. guess) so the
   behaviour change is observable.

## Verification / Definition of Done

- New tests fail before the change and pass after (TDD), and the full
  `proxy/tests/test_usage_limit_reset.py` file passes unchanged (AC2).
- `quota_state` remains a pure cache read on the request path (no polling, no
  blocking, never raises) — verified by the existing `quota_state` tests plus
  the new stale/absent cases.
- `wl update` stage → `in_review` with the retirement documented in this item.

## Deliverables

- Authoritative reset for opencode quarantine
- Removed/retired guessing path for these accounts
- Regression evidence

## Notes

Discovered during planning of LP-0MVF4FIP1001RD8P (producer decision Q3 →
option 3a: out of scope there, tracked here). discovered-from:LP-0MVF4FIP1001RD8P

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers (plan session 2026-10-20)

Plan pre-check: effort **Extra Small**, risk **Low** → below the planning
threshold, so this item was completed via the auto-complete review path
(six review stages + AC-coverage review) rather than a full decomposition.

- Q: "AC1 says *the snapshot's* `seconds_to_reset`. `QuotaSnapshot` exposes an
  account-level (monthly) value and per-window values (`rolling`, `weekly`,
  `monthly`), and a `GoUsageLimitError` may name the exhausted window via
  `metadata.limitName`. Which is authoritative for the quarantine?"
  Answer: not yet supplied by the producer. Working assumption (AC1 read
  literally): the account-level `snapshot.seconds_to_reset` (monthly window) is
  used, matching how surge and `available_times` already treat that value
  (`docs/dev/quota-surge.md` §Derivation rules). **OPEN QUESTION** (producer) —
  matters because a weekly-limit 429 would quarantine for the monthly reset
  (up to ~30 days) instead of the weekly reset (≤7 days), a materially longer
  block.
- Q: "AC1 says *+ configured margin*. Today the margin is the module constant
  `_USAGE_LIMIT_RESET_MARGIN_SECONDS = 120` (not configurable). Is a new config
  key in scope?"
  Answer: not yet supplied. Working assumption: reuse the existing 2-minute
  constant (no new config key, no config-docs change). **OPEN QUESTION**
  (producer) — if a configurable margin is intended, this item grows to include
  `proxy/proxy/quota_state.py`-style key handling and the configuration-keys
  docs.
- Q: "When the gateway message *does* carry an explicit `Resets in ...`
  duration, does the snapshot still win for `opencode-*` accounts?"
  Answer: not yet supplied. Working assumption: yes — the snapshot wins for a
  fresh snapshot (AC1 says "exactly the snapshot's `seconds_to_reset`"), and the
  message/guess cascade remains for non-`opencode-*` entries and stale/absent
  snapshots. **OPEN QUESTION** (producer) — the alternative (explicit message
  wins over the snapshot) is defensible since both are authoritative; the
  choice changes AC1's expected value.

# Intake brief: re-evaluate `session_slot_pool_size` using historical GPU busy-time and contention metrics

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the local slot-pool size (`session_slot_pool_size`, fixed at
**2** since LP-0MV9UNGEB009XUZ5 / LP-0MVCGYAI80084PCZ) re-decided on measured
evidence, so the GPU is sized to the real concurrent demand rather than to a
2026-10-17 snapshot.

## Problem statement

The N=2 verdict was made when the binding constraints were believed to be
(a) queue-timeout rate under 3 concurrent sessions (N=1: 70.6–75%, N=2: 20–25%)
and (b) N=3's per-slot context clamp (83,285). Both premises are now questionable:

1. **Demand exceeds the pool far more often than assumed.** From
   `/var/log/llama-proxy` for 2026-10-19 07:23 → 2026-10-20 07:23 (348 sessions,
   17,580 requests), reconstructing per-session in-flight intervals:
   - peak concurrent sessions with an in-flight request: **7**
   - mean concurrency **2.15**; **37.2% of minutes had >2** concurrent sessions
   - by session class, peak concurrency: `herdr-*` panes **6**, `audit-*` subagents
     **3**, operator/pi/LAN sessions **4**
2. **The pool refuses work while the GPU is not decoding**: `local_dispatch_denied`
   **2,641** times (2,633 with `active=2`), `local_lease_active` skips 1,949,
   contention-queue waits 5,805, of which **4,947 fell back remote** and only 855
   dispatched after the wait.
3. **The reported busy figure understates GPU work.** The report's 29.3% busy
   counts only `Stream started → Stream finished`. Local prefill is logged
   separately as `dispatch_first_byte_ms` and totals **14.3 h** across 463 local
   requests (median 61.8 s, p90 269.8 s, max 817 s). Adding prefill to the 7 h 47 m
   of decode puts real slot occupancy at roughly **79,500 s ≈ 46% of the 48
   slot-hours** available, not 16%.
4. **The queue timeout is shorter than a typical local slot hold.** Median
   dispatch→first-byte is 61.8 s, so a 120 s contention-queue wait
   (`contention_queue_max_wait_seconds: 120`) very often expires before a slot
   frees — consistent with 4,947 queue abandonments vs 855 queue dispatches.

## Task

Produce an evidence-backed slot-count decision (N=2 baseline vs N=3, and N=4 if
memory allows) from the historical record, not a fresh guess.

### Data sources to mine

- `~/proxy-usage-reports/` — **157 archived daily reports** (`YYYY-MM-DD[_n]/report.md`)
  spanning slot-config eras (fast=1/cheap=3 → converged 2). Each carries busy time
  (total / fast / cheap), `Queued → dispatched local`, `Fallback after queue`,
  local-serve share, and decode/prompt-eval speed. Sample already extracted:
  2026-09-01 62.1% busy / 39 queued-dispatched; 2026-10-09 91.6% / 9,556;
  2026-10-14 30.3% / —; 2026-10-17 18.8%; 2026-10-19 68.9%; 2026-10-20 29.3% / 855.
- `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log*` (7-day retention) — per-request
  `dispatch_first_byte_ms`, `local_dispatch_denied`, `contention_queue_*`,
  `lease_*`, `routing_skip_local`.
- `docs/slot-count-verdict-lp-0mv9ungeb009xuz5.md` — the N=2 sweep method and its
  fidelity caveats (must be reused so the new run is comparable).
- llama-server logs for eval/decode timings (largely absent this window — see the
  separate prefill-aware-metrics item).

### Acceptance criteria

1. A historical table of at least 20 archived report days with columns: date, slot
   config in force, mode split, GPU busy %, decode-vs-prefill split where
   available, `local_dispatch_denied`, queue depth/waits, `fallback_after_queue`,
   local serve share. Committed under `docs/` with the extraction script.
2. A concurrency-vs-capacity statement derived from logs: minutes-at-N-concurrent
   distribution, peak, and the share of demand that would still be denied at N=2
   vs N=3 vs N=4.
3. A measured N=3 (and N=4 if feasible) sweep using the same harness as the prior
   verdict, recording: local TTFT (`dispatch_first_byte_ms`), decode tok/s,
   queue-timeout rate, denials, `finish_reason=length` count, llama-server
   startup/`--parallel` agreement, per-slot KV memory and system MemAvailable.
4. A recorded decision (keep N=2 / move to N=3 / N=4) that states the expected
   effect on: local serve share, queue abandonment rate, per-slot context clamp
   (126,976 at N=2 vs 83,285 at N=3 — and therefore the interacting warm-threshold
   item), and VRAM headroom. If the decision is "keep N=2", enumerate the
   mitigations it depends on.
5. No change is made to production slot counts in this item — the deliverable is
   the decision record plus a follow-up item (if the decision is to change N).

## Risks / notes

- N=3 shrinks per-slot context to 83,285, which interacts directly with the
  "warm threshold = 95% of per-slot" item: at N=3 that target becomes 83,012, i.e.
  roughly today's effective ceiling. The two items must be decided together.
- Slots must match llama-server `--parallel` (`start-llama.sh`/`LLAMA_PARALLEL`);
  a mismatch silently wastes or breaks slots (documented in `proxy/config.yaml`).
- Prior sweeps could not isolate local decode share because live sessions held the
  dispatch leases; the new run must hold the mode lock / drain evidence or record
  the same validity caveat.

# Intake brief: seed `cached_ratio` from the persisted local slot snapshot

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want a session that already has a warm prefix in a saved local
slot snapshot to be scored as **warm** at routing time, so it is not bypassed to
remote on the false assumption that its whole prompt must be pre-filled again.

## Problem statement

The cold-cache gate derives `new_tokens = estimated_tokens × (1 − cached_ratio)`,
where `cached_ratio` comes only from `_last_cached_ratio` — an in-memory dict keyed
`(model, session)` that is written **solely** from `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`
on a *previous local response* (`provider.py::_get_cached_ratio`, default `0.0`).

Consequences measured in the window 2026-10-19 07:23 → 2026-10-20 07:23:

- **82.8%** of routing decisions had `cached_ratio=0.00` (5,627 of 6,799), i.e. the
  proxy almost always assumes a full cold prefill.
- Any session crossing 38,000 tokens is therefore permanently bypassed
  (`large_context_bypass`, 1,284 events), even when a slot snapshot for it exists and
  would let llama-server reuse its KV prefix.
- The proxy **already persists and restores slot state**: `session_slot_save_path`
  / `LLAMA_SLOT_SAVE_PATH` (`lifecycle.py`), `_restore_slot_snapshot` and `slot_save`
  (`router.py`), plus `/slots` polling that reads `n_past` / `kv_cache_tokens`
  (`observability.py`, `router_helpers.py`). The information needed to score a
  session as warm is available and simply is not used by the router.
- The in-memory dict is also lost on every proxy restart, so restarts reset the
  whole fleet to "cold" (3 manual restarts in the window), even though the KV
  snapshots survive on disk.

## Proposed change

At session (re)attach — and whenever a local dispatch is about to be gated — seed the
routing ratio from persisted/observed slot state:

1. On `_restore_slot_snapshot` success (or on first request of a session with an
   existing snapshot), read the slot's cached token count (`n_past` /
   `kv_cache_tokens`) and record
   `cached_ratio = min(1.0, cached_tokens / estimated_tokens)` for
   `(model, session)`, with a documented safety margin (only count tokens that are a
   true prefix of the incoming prompt; never assume more than the observed value).
2. Label the source in logs (`cache_state=restored` vs `warm` vs `cold`) so the
   report can separate restored-prefix wins from genuine cache hits.
3. Persist the ratio alongside the slot snapshot so a proxy restart does not reset
   warmness to 0 (optional, if the snapshot itself is authoritative).

## Acceptance criteria

1. A session with a restored slot snapshot whose `n_past` covers ≥ the cold threshold
   fraction no longer emits `routing_skip_local ... reason=large_context_bypass`.
2. Correctness guard: a snapshot that does **not** prefix-match the incoming prompt
   (changed system prompt / truncated history) must not be credited — either detect
   it (prefix hash) or fall back to `cached_ratio=0`; a test covers the mismatch case.
3. Never over-credit: `cached_ratio` from restoration is capped by the measured
   `cached_tokens / estimated_tokens`; a unit test asserts the cap.
4. Logs distinguish `cache_state=restored`; `proxy-usage-analysis` can report restored
   vs cold counts (coordinate with LP-0MVGCQ421005IXGC).
5. Before/after over ≥24h: share of routing decisions with `cached_ratio=0`
   (baseline 82.8%), `large_context_bypass` count (baseline 1,284), local serve share
   (baseline 2.6%), and local `dispatch_first_byte_ms` percentiles (a restored hit
   must show materially lower prefill time, baseline median 61.8 s).
6. Works across a proxy restart: a session resuming after restart is scored warm when
   its snapshot is present and valid.

## Risks / notes

- Wrong credits cause a **full re-prefill anyway** (correctness is preserved, latency
  is not) — hence AC2's prefix check.
- llama.cpp can invalidate its own checkpoints (`forcing full prompt re-processing`
  is expected on this hybrid-architecture Qwen3 per `AGENTS.md`); a restored snapshot
  is not a guarantee of a zero-cost prefix. Measure, do not assume.
- `slot_save failed` (5 events in the window, ReadTimeout) shows save/restore is not
  always reliable; the change must degrade to today's behaviour on failure.

# Intake brief: idle-aware local admission (serve large/cold prompts when the GPU is idle)

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want an oversized (or cache-cold) prompt to be admitted to the local
model **when the GPU has demonstrably been idle**, so idle capacity is spent instead
of a paid remote call.

## Problem statement

Routing is purely size/economics-driven and ignores whether the backend is doing
anything. So a prompt is bypassed even while both slots sit unused for minutes, and
requests are refused for slot occupancy even when the GPU never produced a token.

Measured window 2026-10-19 07:23 → 2026-10-20 07:23:

- Local compute was 7h47m of 48 slot-hours (decode only) and report busy 29.3%; with
  prefill included (`dispatch_first_byte_ms` sum **14.3 h**) real occupancy is ≈46%,
  i.e. the GPU is still idle more than half the window.
- `local_dispatch_denied` **2,641** (2,633 with both slots held), yet the 04:00–05:00
  hour logged **187** denials while local busy was **2.5%**.
- `proxy/config.yaml` already records the same finding from an earlier analysis:
  "Log analysis (5.3h, 198 local_dispatch_denied events) showed **100% of denies
  caused by idle lease holders, never GPU saturation** (active>=3: 0)", with
  inter-turn reclaim gaps of median 0.2 s / p95 1.6 s.
- Both `large_context_bypass` (1,284) and a share of `context_too_large` (2,463) skips
  therefore go remote while the model is idle — the exact inversion of the intended
  economics.

## Proposed change

Add an **idle-aware override** to the local routing gate:

1. Track `last_local_activity_ts` (last dispatch, last chunk/first byte, or last
   stream finish; whichever is latest) and expose it on `/llama/local/status`.
2. In `_should_skip_local`, if the backend has been idle longer than
   `local_idle_admit_seconds` (suggested default 60 s) **and** no request is queued,
   return `(False, None)` for the economic band (`large_context_bypass`) and — as a
   separately configurable and default-off step — for a bounded slice above the warm
   threshold.
3. Emit a distinct, greppable log line (`routing_idle_admit reason=… idle_seconds=…`)
   and count it in the report so the effect is auditable.
4. Fail safe: never override when a queue is non-empty, when the last local attempt
   failed, or when the model is loading/switching.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Config knobs `server.local_idle_admit_enabled` (default false) and
   `server.local_idle_admit_seconds` (default 60) are added, documented, and validated
   (non-negative; disabled when the local model is not healthy).
2. Unit tests: idle > threshold + empty queue ⇒ local admitted; idle < threshold ⇒
   today's bypass; queue non-empty ⇒ today's bypass; model loading ⇒ today's bypass.
3. The override is visible in logs and in `proxy-usage-analysis` (a counter for
   idle-admitted requests), and cannot fire while a hold/lease or prefill is in flight.
4. Before/after over ≥24h: local serve share (baseline 2.6%), idle share of the window
   (baseline ~54% of slot-hours), remote fallback count (baseline 17,076), and
   `dispatch_first_byte_ms` percentiles for idle-admitted requests (they will be slow —
   that is expected; record it).
5. No increase in `local_dispatch_denied` and no increase in mid-stream timeouts
   (`ReadTimeout`, `empty_response`) attributable to the override.

## Risks / notes

- An idle-admitted 120K prompt can occupy a slot for many minutes (observed local
  prefill p90 269.8 s, max 817 s), which can block an interactive request that arrives
  one second later. Mitigations to evaluate in the same change: only admit while the
  contention queue is empty *and* the lease pool has a free slot; cap the admitted
  prompt size; prefer `low` priority.
- Overlaps with LP-0MVGCOZMZ003I6PF (warm threshold 95% of per-slot) and the
  `medium` economic-bypass item: this is the "GPU is idle now" complement to those
  static thresholds. Sequence them so each effect is measurable separately.
- Requires a truthful idle signal; see LP-0MVGCQ421005IXGC (prefill-aware metrics) —
  today's "busy" conflates decode-only with real occupancy.

# Intake brief: serialise local prefills so one prefill at a time gets the full GPU

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want at most one local **prefill** to run at a time (while other
slots may keep decoding), so each request's prefill gets full GPU throughput instead
of sharing it — cutting time-to-first-byte roughly in half with no loss of aggregate
throughput.

## Evidence (window 2026-10-19 07:23 → 2026-10-20 07:23, 460 paired local dispatches)

Prefill intervals (`dispatch_first_byte_ms`, reconstructed as `[t − dur, t]`) bucketed
by how many other local prefills overlapped them:

| Overlapping prefills | n | first-byte p50 | throughput (new tok/s, p50) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | 190 | **23.4 s** | **253.8** |
| 1 | 220 | 85.0 s | 156.6 |
| 2 | 48 | 119.7 s | 128.8 |
| 3 | 2 | 222.2 s | 30.9 |

- **47.8% of local prefills (220/460) shared the GPU with at least one other**
  prefill; 50 shared it with two or more.
- Aggregate throughput is **flat** (≈254 → ≈258 tok/s) while per-request throughput
  halves — i.e. concurrency adds latency, not capacity.
- Observed total prefill wall time 50,645 s vs 21,600 s if every request had run at
  the solitary 254 tok/s → **2.3× inflation** from contention plus coded-context read
  cost.

## Proposed change

Add an admission semaphore for the **prefill phase only**:

1. Track per-slot phase from the existing `/slots` poll (`is_processing`,
   `n_past`/`n_prompt_tokens_processed`, coalesced per `SLOTS_POLL_TTL_SECONDS`).
2. Allow at most `server.local_max_concurrent_prefills` (default **1**) requests in
   prefill across the pool; a request whose slot would start a second concurrent
   prefill waits (bounded) or falls back per policy.
3. A slot already decoding does not block another slot's prefill — only
   prefill-vs-prefill is serialised, so decode keeps running in parallel.
4. Emit `prefill_gate_wait_ms` per request and expose the queue depth on
   `/llama/local/status`.

## Acceptance criteria

1. New config knob `server.local_max_concurrent_prefills` (default 1, 0 disables),
   documented, with validation.
2. Unit tests for the gate: second concurrent prefill waits; a decoding slot does not
   block; a request that cannot be admitted within its budget falls back exactly as
   today; disable → current behaviour.
3. Measured effect over ≥24h via `proxy-usage-analysis`: local `dispatch_first_byte_ms`
   p50/p90 (baseline p50 **61.8 s**, p90 **269.8 s**), share of prefills with ≥1
   overlap (baseline 47.8%), local serve share (baseline 2.6%), decode throughput
   (must not regress), and aggregate prefill tokens/s (must not regress).
4. No increase in `downloaded`/queue abandonment (`contention_queue_fallback_after_queue`,
   baseline 4,947) — the gate must not simply move the wait elsewhere.
5. Interaction recorded with the lease system: the gate must never hold a slot while
   the pool is otherwise idle (test covers "single request alone → no added delay").

## Risks / notes

- With 2 slots, serialising prefills means one slot may idle during a long prefill
  while the other decodes; that is the intended trade (throughput is flat anyway).
- Must not starve large prefills: a 7-minute prefill blocks the gate for 7 minutes;
  combine with a prefill-ETA-aware queue (see the admission-guard item) so queued
  requests with no chance of admission fall back immediately.
- Do not confuse this gate with the existing dispatch lease (session-scoped) or the
  contention queue (slot-scoped) — this one is phase-scoped.

# Intake brief: prefill-ETA-aware admission guard (stop starting local work that cannot finish in budget)

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the proxy to refuse local admission — immediately, with a
retryable hint — when the projected prefill wait cannot fit the caller's wait budget,
so requests stop burning up to 120 s in the contention queue only to fall back to
remote anyway, and slots stop starting prefills that will be abandoned.

## Evidence (window 2026-10-19 07:23 → 2026-10-20 07:23)

- Contention queue: **5,805** waits → **855** dispatched after the wait,
  **4,947** (`85%`) abandoned after up to 120 s and then went remote.
- Local prefill reality vs the 120 s queue cap: p50 **61.8 s**, p90 **269.8 s**,
  max **817 s**; projected cost for a 110k-token cold prompt is ~430 s
  (254 new tok/s solitary, 1.1 ms per coded context token).
- So for most queued requests the queue cannot succeed inside its own budget: the
  wait is a guaranteed loss of up to 120 s of client latency.
- Remote comparison: median remote TTFT **27 ms**, p90 **1.4 s** — waiting 120 s to
  maybe avoid a 27 ms call is a bad bet unless the prompt is genuinely cache-warm.

## Proposed change

Before entering the contention queue (and before a dispatch that would start a
second concurrent prefill), compute a **prefill ETA** and compare it with a wait
budget:

```
eta_prefill = est_tokens * coded_ms_per_token + new_tokens * prefill_ms_per_token
              (calibrated from recent local dispatches; window values 1.1 ms and 3.9 ms)
admit  if eta_prefill + decode_remaining <= wait_budget
else   return 429/503 + Retry-After immediately with X-Local-Admission guidance
```

- `wait_budget` = the caller's queue budget (existing
  `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds`) clamped by `X-Priority` semantics: `high`
  never queues (today), `medium`/`low` use the budget.
- Cache-warm requests (high `cached_ratio`) stay admissible because their
  `new_tokens` term is small — locality where it actually pays.
- Publish the estimate (`prefill_eta_seconds`, `queue_eta_seconds`) on
  `/llama/local/status` so dispatchers can pace before launching a session.

## Acceptance criteria

1. ETA calibration is data-driven: per-model/per-context-bucket coefficients derived
   from recent `dispatch_first_byte_ms` samples (rolling window), with sane defaults
   and a fallback to today's behaviour when insufficient samples exist.
2. Admission decision and reason are logged (`local_admission_guard decision=admit|reject
   eta_prefill_s=… budget_s=…`) and counted in the usage report.
3. Unit tests: ETA above budget ⇒ immediate reject with retryable status and
   `Retry-After`; ETA within budget ⇒ unchanged queue behaviour; `high` priority ⇒
   never queues (regression guard); missing calibration ⇒ unchanged behaviour.
4. Measured effect over ≥24h: `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue` (baseline 4,947)
   drops substantially; p50/p90 client-visible latency for guard-rejected requests
   approaches the remote TTFT baseline instead of ~120 s; local serve share does not
   fall below 2.6%; no increase in mid-stream errors.
5. The guard never rejects a request whose `cached_ratio` implies a cheap prefill
   (test with a 90%-cached 100k prompt: admitted).

## Risks / notes

- The ETA is a model, not a measurement: it must be conservative (prefer fallback) and
  must self-correct from observed `dispatch_first_byte_ms` rather than a fixed constant.
- Requires truthful idle/prefill signals; coordinate with the per-slot status item and
  the prefill-serialisation item (both change the wait landscape).
- Rejecting fast is a UX improvement over a silent 120 s stall, but it makes remote
  spend *visible* — record the spend delta so the trade is explicit.
data.title: Prefill-ETA admission guard: stop starting local work that cannot finish in budget

# Publish truthful local capacity on `/llama/local/status` (slot phase + prefill ETA)

## Goal (user story)

As an operator (and as the ContextHub/herdr dispatcher), I want the proxy's status
endpoint to distinguish *generating*, *idle-but-leased*, and *free* slots and to
publish a prefill ETA, so dispatch decisions stop treating a reserved-but-idle GPU as
busy and stop launching sessions that will immediately queue and fall back.

## Evidence (window 2026-10-19 07:23 → 2026-10-20 07:23)

- `local_dispatch_denied` **2,641** (2,633 with `active=2` lease records), yet local
  was decoding only 29.3% of wall clock, and the 04:00–05:00 hour logged **187**
  denials at 2.5% local busy.
- `proxy/config.yaml` already records the same finding from an earlier analysis:
  "Log analysis (5.3h, 198 local_dispatch_denied events) showed **100% of denies
  caused by idle lease holders, never GPU saturation**".
- The dispatcher (`ContextHub/packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`) already prefers
  per-slot detail (`slots[].is_processing`, `owner_session_id`) over the untrusted
  `available_slots` count, and reads `contention_queue_depth` — but a slot held by an
  *inactive* lease is indistinguishable from a working one, and there is no ETA.
  Concretely, `isSlotOwned()` (downtime-worker.ts) treats *any* slot with a non-empty
  `owner_session_id` as busy regardless of `is_processing`, which is exactly the
  false-busy behaviour this item removes.
- Prefill dominates the hold time (p50 61.8 s, p90 269.8 s), so "busy" without an ETA
  is not actionable for a dispatcher that must decide *before* spawning an agent.

## Proposed change

Extend the local status payload (additive, backward compatible — older consumers keep
working):

```json
{
  "slots": [
    {"slot_id": "0", "is_processing": true, "phase": "prefill|decode",
     "owner_session_id": "…", "lease_state": "generating|idle_leased|free",
     "context_tokens": 102345, "prefill_eta_seconds": 187.0}
  ],
  "total_slots": 2, "available_slots": 0,
  "contention_queue_depth": 3, "queue_eta_seconds": 240.0,
  "prefill_budget_seconds": 120,
  "capacity_hint": "saturated|prefill_bound|idle",
  "status_schema_version": 2
}
```

Rules: `lease_state` distinguishes an idle lease from active work; `prefill_eta_seconds`
is derived from the same calibration used by the admission guard; `capacity_hint`
summarises whether the pool is genuinely working.

## Implementation context (from plan review)

Existing building blocks to reuse — this item extends, it does not re-derive:

- `get_llama_local_status()` in `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` is the endpoint; it already
  emits **`prefill_eta_seconds`**, **`queue_eta_seconds`** and
  **`local_owner_lease_remaining_seconds`** (from LP-0MVGDUV5E005UWBQ and
  LP-0MVGD9Z8Z0055Y5J).
- `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py` is the shared calibration / admission guard
  (`estimate_prefill_seconds`, `coefficients`, `wait_budget_seconds`,
  `evaluate_admission`). Per-slot `prefill_eta_seconds` and `prefill_budget_seconds`
  must read from here — never a second estimator.
- `_query_slots_detail()` and `_last_slot_details_cache` in
  `proxy/proxy/observability.py` supply per-slot `is_processing`, `n_decoded`, and the
  prompt progress (`n_past` / `n_prompt_tokens_processed`); `_query_slots()` +
  `last_known_slot_counts()` supply counts and the `SLOT_COUNTS_STALE_AFTER_SECONDS`
  freshness bound; `SLOTS_POLL_TTL_SECONDS` single-flight coalescing must be reused so
  status polling adds no load.
- `proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md` documents the current `slots[]` contract
  — extend it (or add a sibling `proxy/docs/local-status-capacity-contract.md`) rather
  than starting a new document family.

Decisions taken (see Appendix): `phase` is inferred **proxy-side** (no upstream
llama.cpp field is required), and `capacity_hint` uses the decision table in AC4.

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` — `get_llama_local_status()`; add `phase`, `lease_state`, `context_tokens`, `prefill_budget_seconds`, `capacity_hint`, `status_schema_version`.
- `proxy/proxy/observability.py` — `_query_slots_detail()`, `_last_slot_details_cache`, `_query_slots()`, `last_known_slot_counts()`; per-slot signals and staleness.
- `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py` — shared calibration / admission guard; single source for every ETA.
- `proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md` — existing `slots[]` contract; extend with the new fields.
- `proxy/tests/test_llama_local_status.py` — endpoint payload tests; add new-field, `lease_state`, `capacity_hint`, staleness and old-shaped-consumer contract tests.
- `ContextHub/packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — consumer parser notes pointer only (code change is a ContextHub item).

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-20 (plan skill): intake brief converted to an implementation-ready plan after a
  producer interview (3 questions: `capacity_hint` table, `phase` source, measurement
  placement). AC3 scoped as a *reuse* requirement against `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py`;
  AC5 (`phase` inference) and AC7 (staleness honesty) added; old AC6 (correlated
  measurement) moved out of scope to the separate item `LP-0MVGR2OXT0096OGK`; Key Files
  and implementation-context sections added.

## Acceptance criteria

1. New fields are additive and versioned (`status_schema_version` or equivalent); a
   client that ignores them behaves exactly as today (contract test with an
   old-shaped consumer).
2. `lease_state` is correct in all three cases, including a session holding an inactive
   lease after its stream finished (test), and never reports `free` while a prefill or
   decode is in flight.
3. **Reuse requirement:** per-slot `prefill_eta_seconds` and top-level
   `queue_eta_seconds` / `prefill_budget_seconds` are sourced from the existing shared
   calibration in `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py` (one source of truth with the admission
   guard — no second estimator), and are `null` when not computable rather than a
   misleading `0`.
4. `capacity_hint` is documented with its exact decision table and unit-tested. Table,
   evaluated in order: `idle` when at least one slot is free **or** every occupied slot
   is `idle_leased`; `prefill_bound` when no slot is free and at least one occupied slot
   is in `prefill`; `saturated` when no slot is free and every occupied slot is in
   `decode`.
5. `phase` is inferred proxy-side from `/slots` signals (`is_processing`,
   `next_token.n_decoded`, prompt progress): `prefill` while prompt progress advances
   without `n_decoded` advancing (or `is_processing` with `n_decoded` ≈ 0), `decode`
   otherwise, and `null` when the slot is not processing. Unit-tested for both phases
   and the not-processing case.
6. Documented consumer contract in `proxy/docs/` (and a pointer from
   `ContextHub/packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`'s parser notes) so the dispatcher
   can gate on `lease_state` and `prefill_eta_seconds`.
7. Freshness honesty: `slots_stale` semantics are preserved, and both per-slot and
   top-level ETA fields are `null` (not stale numbers) when the underlying `/slots`
   poll is stale (test).

Out of scope (moved to a separate item, not a child): the post-deploy correlated
measurement of denials-per-hour versus local busy — see
`LP-0MVGR2OXT0096OGK` (Measure whether lease_state/prefill_eta predict real local
contention).

## Risks / notes

- Status polling must not add load: reuse the existing `/slots` coalescing
  (`SLOTS_POLL_TTL_SECONDS`, single-flight).
- Do not expose stale data as fresh: keep `slots_stale` semantics and mark ETA `null`
  when the underlying `/slots` poll is stale.
- The consumer change (herdr gating on the new fields) lives in ContextHub and is a
  separate item there; this item only guarantees the contract.
- `phase` inference is heuristic for very short prefills (single-tick); the `null`
  fallback is preferred over a wrong guess.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "`capacity_hint` decision table (AC4)? Proposed: `idle` when a slot is free or all
  occupied slots are `idle_leased`; `prefill_bound` when nothing is free and ≥1 slot is
  prefilling; `saturated` when nothing is free and all occupied slots are decoding."
  Answer (producer): **A — adopt exactly this table**. Final: accepted, recorded as AC4.
- Q: "`phase` source? (A) infer proxy-side from `/slots` signals, (B) parse
  llama-server log progress lines, (C) block on an upstream llama.cpp field."
  Answer (producer): **A — infer proxy-side**. Evidence: `_query_slots_detail()`
  already parses `is_processing`, `next_token.n_decoded`, `n_past` and
  `n_prompt_tokens_processed` (`proxy/proxy/observability.py`). Final: accepted, AC5.
- Q: "Correlated measurement (old AC6) — keep in this item as post-deploy
  verification, spin out as a child, or docs-only?" Answer (producer): **B — separate
  item entirely, not a child**. Final: created `LP-0MVGR2OXT0096OGK`; this item's ACs
  were renumbered and the measurement removed from scope.
data.title: Publish truthful local capacity on /llama/local/status (slot phase + prefill ETA)

# Intake brief: re-widen local size gates only once cache warmth is proven (capacity-gated)

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I still want large prompts (38K–124K tokens) served locally **when the
GPU can actually absorb them** — but only after cache-warmth work has cut the cost per
request, and with admission sized to measured capacity rather than to a fixed token
threshold.

## Why this replaces the two deleted widening items

The previously filed items — "warm threshold to 95% of per-slot context"
(LP-0MVGCOZMZ003I6PF, deleted) and "economic bypass for medium priority"
(LP-0MVGD9YLM0055SFF, deleted) — were deleted because, as scoped, they widen admission
faster than the GPU can absorb, which makes cache churn and first-token latency worse:

| Band | Requests / 24h | Median prompt | Cold cost at 254 new tok/s | Slot-hours needed | Prefill headroom available |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 100,000–124,518 (`context_too_large`) | 890 | ~110k | ~430 s each | **~107 h** | ~26 h |
| 38,000–100,000 (`large_context_bypass`) | 1,284 | ~71k | ~280 s each | **~100 h** | ~26 h |

Headroom = 48 slot-hours/day − 28,020 s decode − 50,645 s measured prefill ≈ 26 h
(≈23.8 M new tokens at 254 tok/s). Both bands are ~4× over capacity **cold**, and ≈10
slot-hours each at a 90% cache-hit rate — i.e. they fit *only* with warm caches.

## Preconditions (blocking)

1. **Cache warmth**: `cached_ratio` seeded from persisted slot snapshots
   (LP-0MVGD9YXH008O304) — measured by the share of local dispatches that are
   `cache_state=cold` (baseline **45.7%**, 210/460).
2. **Admission control**: prefill-ETA-aware admission guard (the "stop starting local
   work that cannot finish in budget" item) so a widened gate cannot turn into
   queue-then-fallback stalls.
3. **Prefill protection**: prefill serialisation so widened admission does not halve
   per-request prefill throughput via contention (baseline: 47.8% of prefills shared the
   GPU, p50 85 s with one overlap vs 23.4 s alone).

## Proposed change (only after the preconditions land)

Replace the two fixed token thresholds' *effective* behaviour with a **capacity-aware
admission** rule layered on the existing thresholds:

- Keep `context_too_large` as the hard physical cap (`ctx // slots − 4096` = 126,976).
- For the economic band, admit locally while the projected slot-hours of admitted
  traffic stay within a configured share of idle capacity (e.g.
  `local_capacity_admission_budget_ratio: 0.8` of measured idle slot-time), and fall
  back to remote when the projection exceeds it.
- Raise the warm threshold toward 95% of per-slot (124,518 at N=2) **only** as the
  measured cache-hit rate supports it; report the achieved setting.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Preconditions evidenced in comments before implementation starts: cold-dispatch

## Goal

Raise the local warm-context routing cap from 100,000 to 120,000 estimated tokens so that requests in the 100K–120K band are admitted to local routing instead of being bypassed remote, and make the configuration actually bind (the economic-ceiling ratio currently clamps at ~100K, so raising the absolute value alone is a no-op).

## Background (measured 2026-10-20 08:06 → 2026-10-21 08:06)

From the proxy-usage-analysis report (157 sessions, 7,048 requests, 5,541 routing decisions):

- `routing_skip_local` events: 3,249 — `context_too_large` 2,462 (75.8%), `large_context_bypass` 787 (24.2%).
- `context_too_large` = estimated prompt context > warm cap (100,000). These are 44.4% of all routing decisions.
- Local model busy only 21.4% of the window (idle 78.6%), so this is a **context cap** problem, not a capacity problem.
- Warm cap resolves as `min(physical per-slot clamp, economic ceiling)`:
  - physical = `local_model_ctx_size // slots - 4096` (126,976 at 2 slots; 83,285 at 3 slots)
  - economic = `round(0.3815 × 262144)` = 100,001, capped by the absolute `local_large_context_warm_cache_threshold` (100,000)
  - → effective warm cap = **100,000**; raising the absolute value alone yields 100,008 (verified by calling `_effective_large_context_thresholds` against the live config).

## Change required (both parts, else no-op)

1. `server.local_large_context_warm_cache_threshold`: `100000` → `120000`
2. `server.local_large_context_economic_ceiling_ratio`: `0.3815` → `0.4578` (= 120000/262144, so the economic term stops being the binding constraint)

With both changes the effective warm cap is 120,000 whenever the physical per-slot clamp allows it (2 slots → 126,976 OK; 3 slots → 83,285 still binds, so the change is inert while 3 slots are active — documented, expected).

## Expected effect (forecast from the analysis window)

Requests with estimated context in (100K, 120K]: **436** across 26 sessions, of which **175** have `new_tokens <= cold threshold (38,000)` and therefore become genuinely local-eligible; the remaining 261 are cold-cache (`new_tokens > 38,000`) and flip from `context_too_large` to `large_context_bypass` — still remote under the fast profile, since `economic_bypass_serves_local` is off there.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `server.local_large_context_warm_cache_threshold` is 120000 and `server.local_large_context_economic_ceiling_ratio` is 0.4578 in `proxy/config.yaml`, with comments explaining that both must move together and how the 3-term model resolves.
2. `_effective_large_context_thresholds` returns warm = 120000 at 2 slots and warm = 83285 at 3 slots for the live config (unit test asserting both, so the slot-count interaction is pinned).
3. Unit tests cover the economic-ceiling interaction: a config with `abs=120000`, `ratio=0.4578` yields 120000; the same with the old ratio 0.3815 yields ~100K (regression guard that raising only the absolute value cannot silently no-op again).
4. Documentation updated (`docs/llama-router.md`, `proxy/README.md`, `proxy/docs/routing.md`) to state the 120K warm cap, the ratio and why they move together.
5. Test fixtures referencing the old values (`proxy/tests/fixtures/merged_config_{fast,cheap}.json`, `prededup_raw_{fast,cheap}.json`) updated where they assert live-config values, or confirmed intentionally independent.
6. Full proxy test suite passes.

## Dependency

Blocked by / depends on LP-0MSEGPO77005CYCQ (token-estimate multiplier / native-tokenizer fix) — the cap is expressed in *estimated* tokens, so its calibration is only meaningful once the routing estimate matches Qwen3-native tokenisation. That item is completed (shipped v0.1.10; native `tokenizer: qwen3` is live in config), so this work is unblocked.

## User story

As an operator running many concurrent agent sessions against a 2-slot local
Qwen3 backend, I need a session that already holds (or has just released) a
local dispatch lease to be re-admitted ahead of a newcomer, so that a
returning session does not burn the full contention-queue budget and detour
to a paid remote provider — and then come back and re-prefill — repeatedly
within a single session.

## Observed behaviour (routing thrash)

Session `audit-WL-0MVFRRKKN00544PQ-phase2_child_5-6e22ef57` (2026-10-21,
12:23:35–12:36:55) alternated local ↔ remote **7 times in 12 minutes**:

| # | time | provider | trigger |
|---|------|----------|---------|
| 1 | 12:24:29 | local Qwen3 | `contention_queue_dispatch queued_duration=48.37s` |
| 2 | 12:25:27 | local Qwen3 | `contention_queue_dispatch queued_duration=48.96s` |
| 3 | 12:27:30 | MunitoAI Free | `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue queued_duration=120.00s` |
| 4 | 12:28:06 | local Qwen3 | reclaim, `cached_ratio=0.513`, 35.8 s prefill |
| 5 | 12:30:30 | OpenCode Go 3 | `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue queued_duration=120.00s` |
| 6 | 12:34:43 | OpenCode Go 3 | `local_dispatch_denied ... owner=audit-WL-0MVFRRMX3003UPP3-phase2_child_6 active=1` |
| 7 | 12:34:48 | local Qwen3 | reclaim, `cached_ratio=0.396`, 2.2 s prefill |

Every hop was **not** a context-size or ETA-guard decision: the
`local_admission_guard` returned `decision=admit reason=within_budget` at
3.9 s / 9.8 s / 11.0 s / 66.7 s / 72.9 s on every attempt, and prompts were
only 2,067–20,468 tokens (far below `local_large_context_cold_cache_threshold`
38000). The binding constraint was **dispatch contention**: the slot was held
by another session (`local_lease_active`, `local_dispatch_denied owner=<other
session>`), so the request waited the full `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds`
(120 s) and then fell through to the remote chain.

Cost per hop: a wasted 120 s queue wait, a paid remote round-trip, plus a
re-prefill on return (35.8 s at 12:28:06, 2.2 s at 12:34:48). It also erodes
the session's own cached-prefix bookkeeping (`cached_ratio` fell 0.513 → 0.396
across one remote detour).

## Root cause hypothesis

The contention queue orders by arrival, not by cache locality or prior lease
ownership. A session that has just released its local lease (`lease_released
reason=idle_timeout`) and immediately returns re-queues behind newcomers, even
though its KV prefix is still resident and its own prefill would be far
cheaper than a newcomer's cold prefill. With 2 slots and 3+ active sessions
this starves returning sessions deterministically.

## Proposed fix

1. **Lease-owner retention priority** — a session with an active lease, or one
   released within a configurable grace window (e.g.
   `contention_queue_lease_grace_seconds`), is dispatched ahead of a session
   with no local cache history in the contention queue.
2. **Skip the futile wait** — when a returning session is queued behind a
   newcomer whose prefill will not finish inside the returning session's
   budget, refuse immediately (as the prefill-ETA guard already does for
   over-budget ETAs) instead of waiting the full 120 s.
3. **Observability** — emit a log line when the retention priority reorders
   the queue, so the behaviour is auditable and countable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1: A session with an active local lease, or a lease released within
      `contention_queue_lease_grace_seconds` (new config knob, default
      documented), is dispatched ahead of a newcomer in the contention queue;
      the reorder emits a log line naming both sessions and the reason.
- [ ] AC2: Unit test: session A takes and releases a local lease, session B
      queues with no cache history, A returns — A is dispatched first. Asserted
      on dispatch order, and the log line from AC1 is present.
- [ ] AC3: Unit test: a returning session whose prefix has genuinely been
      evicted (no cached-ratio record, no slot sidecar) is not held ahead of a
      newcomer and still falls through without burning the full
      `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds`.
- [ ] AC4: Regression test: when the prefill-ETA guard refuses admission
      (`eta_exceeds_budget`), the remote fallback still happens immediately —
      no new queue wait is introduced by the priority change.
- [ ] AC5: The routing-thrash pattern is measurable: the proxy-usage report (or
      an equivalent aggregate) counts local↔remote provider transitions per
      session, so the 7-hop case above is detectable without manual log
      archaeology.
- [ ] AC6: Replaying/observing the recorded case (or a synthetic equivalent)
      shows fewer than 3 provider transitions where 7 occurred before.
- [ ] AC7: `config.yaml` documents the new knob(s) with the default and a
      rollback path; changed-scope tests and the full suite pass.

## Related finding (separate item)

The second turn of this session also routed with `cached_ratio=0.00` despite
turn 1 having completed locally — the ratio is recorded from the *previous*
response's measured `cached_tokens`, so a genuinely cold first turn writes
0.0 and turn 2 inherits it. See the accompanying `discovered-from` item.

## User story

As an operator, I need the proxy's per-session `cached_ratio` (used by both
routing and the prefill-ETA admission guard) to predict the *next* prompt's
reusable prefix, not just report the hit fraction of the *previous* one, so
that the second turn of a session is not scored cache-cold straight after a
successful first local turn.

## Observed behaviour

Session `audit-WL-0MVFRRKKN00544PQ-phase2_child_5-6e22ef57`:
turn 1 dispatched locally at 12:24:29 (2,067 tokens, cache-cold — the first
request ever for this session), then turn 2's `routing_check` at 12:25:20
reported `estimated_tokens=5221 new_tokens=5221 cached_ratio=0.00
cache_state=cold`, even though the turn-1 prefix should still be resident
(and the actual prefill took 6.6 s for 5.2k tokens ≈ 790 tok/s vs 402 tok/s
for the genuinely cold turn 1 — consistent with real prefix reuse that the
bookkeeping did not credit).

## Root cause

`proxy/proxy/provider.py` `update_cached_ratio` records
`cached_tokens/prompt_tokens` **measured on the previous local response**
(`usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`), keyed by session. A genuinely
cold first turn (0/2067 cached) writes **0.0** into
`_last_cached_ratio[(model, session)]`. Every later request reads that 0.0
until a *later* response happens to report a hit — so a cold start poisons
turn 2's routing and prefill-ETA estimate by construction. The 1.0-fallback
on `slot_save success` and the restored-prefix sidecar both require a slot
snapshot, which is rarely taken (5 successes in the whole day's log; never
for this session), so in practice the only writer is the zero-first-turn
usage path.

Impact: the *previous*-prompt hit fraction is the wrong input for the
*next*-prompt cost estimate. For a session that grows by tool results, the
next prompt's expectation is ~tokens(N-1)/tokens(N), not the last hit
fraction. Downstream this inflates `eta_prefill`, can push the ETA guard into
`eta_exceeds_budget` on sessions that would actually re-prefill cheaply, and
undercuts the lease-owner-retention fix in the parent item.

## Proposed fix

Track per-session the last recorded prompt-token count and, at routing time,
derive the expected reusable prefix as the overlap between the previous
prompt and the current one (prefix match on the message list, as the
slot-snapshot sidecar already does), seeded at 0 only when no local dispatch
has ever been observed for the session.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1: A session whose first turn dispatched locally with a cold cache
      shows a non-zero `cached_ratio` on the second turn's `routing_check`
      when the second prompt is a strict superset (prefix match) of the
      first.
- [ ] AC2: A session with no prior local dispatch still routes cold (0.0) —
      no behaviour change for brand-new sessions.
- [ ] AC3: A session whose prompt history changed at the head (different
      system prompt / truncated history) still routes cold — no over-credit.
- [ ] AC4: The prefill-ETA guard's output (`eta_prefill_s`) reflects the
      corrected ratio so a returning session that would re-prefill cheaply is
      not refused with `eta_exceeds_budget`.
- [ ] AC5: Existing behaviour preserved when no usage data is present
      (`source=usage` absent) and when the slot-snapshot path is in play
      (`source=save` / `source=restored` still work as today).
- [ ] AC6: Unit tests cover AC1–AC5; changed-scope tests and the full suite
      pass.

Discovered during the routing-thrash investigation of LP-0MVI2VRT2000V1AP.

## Defect

`contention_queue_lease_grace_seconds` (added by LP-0MVI2VRT2000V1AP) is
clamped by `_get_contention_queue_config` to `[0, contention_queue_max_wait_seconds]`
(120). The shipped config value is **300**, so every call emits:

```
WARNING - contention_queue_lease_grace_seconds=300 clamped to 120.0
          (bounds [0, contention_queue_max_wait_seconds=120.0])
```

`_get_contention_queue_config` runs **per request** (and per status poll), so
the warning fires continuously — measured on the restart at 2026-10-21
14:47: **36 warnings within seconds**. It pollutes the log, will trip
rate-based alerting on the WARNING stream, and contradicts both the
`config.yaml` comment and `docs/dev/contention-queue-lease-retention.md`,
which state 300 s is the default and is deliberately longer than a single
queue budget.

Functional impact is limited (grace 120 still covers one full queue budget,
so retention priority still works), but the default is silently not what the
config promises.

## Root cause

The clamp bound was chosen as "cannot keep priority longer than a full queue
budget", but the intent of the knob is the opposite: it must be **at least**
one full budget (so a returning session always re-queues as retained) and may
legitimately be larger. Clamping to the wait cap makes the configured default
unrepresentable.

## Fix

Clamp to `[0, session_guardrail_max_runtime_seconds]` (already resolved in the
same function, default 1800) — the same ceiling the wait cap uses — so 300 is
valid, `0` still disables retention, and a pathological value is still
bounded. The warning then only fires for genuinely out-of-range values.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1: With `contention_queue_lease_grace_seconds: 300` and
      `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds: 120`, `_get_contention_queue_config`
      returns `lease_grace_seconds == 300.0` and logs **no** warning.
- [ ] AC2: Values above `session_guardrail_max_runtime_seconds` are clamped to
      it with a single warning; `0` disables retention (rollback path) with no
      warning; negative values clamp to 0.
- [ ] AC3: No WARNING is emitted per request for a valid configuration —
      asserted by calling the resolver repeatedly and counting warnings (the
      regression this item exists for).
- [ ] AC4: `config.yaml` comment and
      `docs/dev/contention-queue-lease-retention.md` state the corrected
      bounds and agree with the code.
- [ ] AC5: Existing contention-queue, retention and config tests stay green;
      changed-scope tests pass.

Discovered during the proxy restart that activated LP-0MVI2VRT2000V1AP.
